newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Brokers dismiss Lion takeover rumours.
newsitem.headline: Brokers dismiss Lion takeover rumours.

text.p: Market speculation that Australasian brewer Lion Nathan is a takeover target has driven its share price higher but there is little substance to it, New Zealand brokers said on Thursday.
Lion shares closed on Thursday at NZ$4.00, their highest level since March, 1994. They have gained 25 cents since the start of this month.
Brokers said rumours were circulating the market that Lion was ripe for a corporate swoop, but gave them little credence. They said it was an old story which resurfaced from time to time.

"When the stock gets up to these higher prices, these sorts of things get trotted out again. I don't know of any legitimate stories with regard to corporate deals," said Sean Vaughan at County Natwest.
"The rumour is being bought at the moment -- we haven't seen the selling of the fact yet."

He noted that the brewer had reportedly increased its market share in Australia and said it was also a beneficiary of the weaker kiwi dollar, which has plunged against the greenback and the Aussie dollar over the past six weeks.
"There's good two-way business, so there's obviously people taking distinct views either way," Vaughan said.
He said if the stock broke above the $4.00 mark, it could rally another 10 or 20 cents, but if the takeover rumours came to nothing, it was also just as likely to retreat.
"We've seen the stock move up on speculative rumours before and come back again, and I think this may just be another one of those examples."
Lion executives were not immediately available to comment.
